final.memo:
Potlatch represents a classic case of a company squandering valuable timber assets to fund a struggling, capital-intensive manufacturing operation that destroys shareholder wealth. While the company faces a cyclical downturn, management's decision to press forward with a $66 million investment in a Las Vegas towel plant during a supply glut is an unacceptable misuse of capital that underscores a fundamental lack of discipline [D01]. The company's own data confirms the severity of this mismanagement, with a 2002 return on equity of negative 33.1% compared to negative 4.1% for the peer group [D02].

Management attempts to justify this 'empire building' by pointing to future industry cycles, but shareholders cannot afford to subsidize this optimism indefinitely [D01, D06]. The existing governance structure, which utilizes a staggered board and high voting hurdles to shield directors, acts as a barrier to the necessary strategic shift [D03, D07]. We must move beyond private engagement and escalate our opposition publicly. The goal is to force a separation of the timber assets from the manufacturing business and demand a cessation of all non-essential capital projects.

Third Point is already the seventh-largest shareholder, and our position as an active participant in this annual cycle gives us the platform to challenge the current board's inertia [D07]. We will not wait for the long-term industry recovery while management continues to erode the value of the underlying assets. We require an immediate commitment to portfolio simplification and a governance refresh to restore the value that our 3% stake is entitled to [D07, D08].
